newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil swaps - CFDs ease off, mogas, fuel climb.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil swaps - CFDs ease off, mogas, fuel climb.

text.p: European oil swaps were a mixed bag on Friday - Brent CFDs eased off a couple of cents, but gasoline and fuel gained while naphtha was unchanged to very narrowly easier.

Brent CFDs slipped a touch with June 2-6 hovering around -32/33 cents against July compared with -30/31 on Thursday. Further out weeks were also weaker by one to two cents. A June 2-6 was heard done at August -44 cents while first half June dated Brent was offered at July -25 cents.

High sulphur fuel swaps edged up a touch, but low sulphur swaps ticked down a little. Several high sulphur June swaps were done at $83.25, $83.50 and $83.75 with July offered around $84.75 and around $84. Low sulphur eased back a touch with June pegged around $93.50.

Gasoline swaps tracked higher on the back of stronger screen numbers on Thursday with June valued around $207 from $204.50 the previous day. July continues to show a $6 backwardation with August a further $2-2.50 backwardated. Traders said gasoline was looking stronger into next week with the API draw giving some support.
The UK budget, which many dealers think will contain higher gasoline excise, will be announced on Monday making a late June, early July date more likely than the previously anticipated June 10.
Naphtha swaps were about 25 cents off with June hovering around $188 and July about $189.
"It's very slow today," commented one naphtha dealer.
